results.title: ChatGPT Launches a Version of Its Model for Teens - CNET
results.content:
OpenAI announced Tuesday that it’s launching a version of ChatGPT intended for teenagers, amid concerns about how younger people interact with generative AI tools.

Users between the ages of 13 and 17 will automatically use the teen-specific version, which will feature parental controls, stronger safeguards and notifications prompting them to take breaks. Many AI companies, including Google, allow people aged 13 or older to use their chatbots, while Anthropic requires users to be 18 or older.

OpenAI says it created ChatGPT for Teens with four guidelines in mind:  “put teen safety first, encourage real-world support, treat teens like teens and be transparent about how our systems should behave.” [...] Makers of AI chatbots have faced widespread questions and criticism over a lack of guardrails in their products, which many people use every day.

The protections now being folded into chatbots are similar to those built into Instagram teen accounts.

## The teen experience in ChatGPT

OpenAI says its model for teens is intended to “expand educational opportunity” and to provide support outside the classroom.

ChatGPT for Teens includes a new Study Mode that provides step-by-step guidance on concepts and homework materials, while also detecting when students attempt to use the model as a shortcut for cheating. With the Study Hours feature, teenage students and parents can set parameters to have Study Mode turn on by default. [...] ChatGPT for Teens will also feature quizzes and visualizations intended to support learning.

“Not every student has someone at home who can help when they get stuck or have questions with their homework. With the right guardrails, AI can help fill that gap,” Racquel Gibson, a Miami high-school math teacher, said in OpenAI’s blog post about ChatGPT for Teens.

ChatGPT for Teens includes built-in protections against overuse and is designed to help prevent emotional dependency, including the chatbot becoming a substitute for real-world companionship and relationships. A survey released last year by Common Sense Media found that 72% of teens regularly use chatbots for companionship and advice.

ChatGPT for Teens turns the AI chatbot into a learning tool for young users. Credit: Ian Moore/Mashable/OpenAI

The majority of teens use artificial intelligence, including ChatGPT, for schoolwork and entertainment"). Now OpenAI has created a new dedicated product for them: ChatGPT for Teens.

This customizable version of ChatGPT, which debuted Tuesday, is designed to "support" learning and human relationships, according to OpenAI's launch announcement. It will be the default experience for any self-identified teen or users who OpenAI estimate are between the ages of 13 and 17.

results.title: ChatGPT is getting a dedicated mode for teens - OpenAI
results.content:
OpenAI is introducing a dedicated ChatGPT mode for teenagers, combining existing youth safeguards and new safety features under one roof. The launch comes amid mounting public scrutiny over how AI tools affect younger users, as other platforms implement their own age checks and teen-specific protections.

ChatGPT for Teens is “an experience designed to help teens learn, think critically, deepen understanding, and use AI with confidence,” OpenAI said in a blog post published Tuesday. Teen mode will automatically apply to users who identify themselves as being between the ages of 13 and 17, as well as those the system estimates to be under 18. Children under 13 aren’t permitted to use the platform, according to OpenAI’s published age policy.
